subject: Radiology
title: Trauma Radiology: FAST Exam & Head CT Rules
preview: FAST/eFAST provides rapid point-of-care ultrasound clues in trauma, but negative views do not exclude every important injury.

sections.title: What FAST is designed to detect
points: Focused views assess the pericardial region and dependent abdominal spaces for free fluid.
An unstable trauma patient may require urgent action despite incomplete imaging.

sections.title: What extended FAST adds
points: Assess lung sliding and other ultrasound signs in the correct anatomical context; no single sign is sufficient in every patient.
Use full trauma assessment and definitive imaging when indicated in stable patients.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A negative FAST does not exclude retroperitoneal injury or every intra-abdominal injury.
A normal lung sliding assessment is not a universal rule-out test for all chest emergencies.

quickRevision: FAST looks for free intraperitoneal or pericardial fluid in a trauma setting.
Extended FAST adds thoracic ultrasound observations to assess selected chest injuries including pneumothorax or hemothorax.
Performance depends on operator skill, timing, imaging windows and clinical context.

quiz.question: What does eFAST help detect during trauma assessment?
options: Free fluid and selected thoracic emergencies
quiz.explanation: FAST/eFAST uses ultrasound to seek free fluid and selected chest complications rapidly; a negative study cannot rule out every traumatic injury.
